correctness.rationale: The exact labeled domains for one, three, and five voters are exhausted, and an independent anonymous multiplicity census covers all 252 five-voter anonymous profiles. Two Kemeny formulations agree profile by profile; the weighted anonymous divergence total is exactly 180; all six anonymous divergences form one candidate orbit.

evidence: Courtin–Mbih–Moyouwou define Copeland and Kemeny, and prove Kemeny is equivalent to maximin for three candidates.
Brandt–Dong–Peters place Kemeny in the maximin cluster below Copeland in the three-candidate refinement diagram and state that Copeland returns all candidates on a tie-free majority cycle.
The public minimal-tilted-cycle source proves that five voters and cyclic margins \((3,1,1)\) are the first odd tie-free separation shape.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These sources establish the rule relationship and the margin-level boundary. They do not determine how many preference profiles realize that boundary or whether all realizations are one candidate-symmetry type.

value.rationale: The first odd Kemeny–Copeland separation is a canonical comparison between a margin-sensitive Condorcet rule and a win-count rule. The exact realization theorem supplies both natural probability-model incidences and a structural one-orbit classification, showing that every first conflict is the same preference-profile phenomenon up to candidate symmetry.
